Theme

Latin word

utervīs

utervīs, utravīs, utrumvīs

pronoun and adjective; uter declines, -vīs stays

either of two, whichever you like; whichever (of two) you like, either

In this lexicon

  • either

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 10: quī utramvīs rēctē nōrit, ambās nōverit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 33: minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs (Lewis & Short)

  • whichever

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 33: at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs; Ter. Haut. 342: in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē ut dormiās

Examples

  • tange utramvīs digitulō minimō modo

    just touch either of them with your little fingerPlaut. Rud. 3.4.15 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for either

  • at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs

    but I have less strength than either of youCic. Sen. 33 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for either

  • in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē dormīre

    to sleep soundly on either ear (without a care)Ter. Heaut. 342 (Lewis & Short, Heaut. 2.3.101)

    In the entry for either
